credentials.title: Credentials
credentials.description: A read-only account is enough and recommended.

error.url_credentials: Do not put a username or password in the URL - they are asked for in the next step.
error.invalid_url: Invalid URL; expected http:// or https://.
error.not_influxdb: Something other than InfluxDB answered at this URL (e.g. a login page).

init.title: Measurements and limits
init.description: The proxy has to read from the same measurements (InfluxDB tables) that Home Assistant's InfluxDB integration writes to. Copy the settings you have there - otherwise the charts stay empty.

data_description.measurement_mode: Unit: all temperatures in "°C", humidity in "%" - what Home Assistant does unless you changed it. entity_id: every entity in its own measurement. Domain and device class: e.g. "sensor__temperature".
data_description.default_measurement: For entities the rule above gives no name for, e.g. without a unit (on/off states, modes). Same as "default_measurement" in the InfluxDB integration, often "state". Empty = the entity_id.
data_description.override_measurement: Reads every entity from this one measurement and ignores the rules above. Same as "override_measurement" in the InfluxDB integration. Usually empty.
data_description.max_entities: How many entities a card may fetch at once - a guard against overloading the database.
data_description.max_days: How far back one request may go (800 days = about 2 years).
data_description.max_state_rows: Raw state changes (/states endpoint): at most this many rows per entity in one request; when a range has more, the newest are kept. A busy motion sensor writes ~700 a day.

options.domain_device_class: Domain and device class, e.g. sensor__temperature
